Figured I'd put this here, what's the best free editing software you can think of off the top of your head?

1) What editing software do you recommend?

Editing softwares are just tools to get what you need done. Whatever tool gets in your way the least is what you should use. Try them all out. See which one is the easiest for YOU. I personally like Adobe Premier (it's also the most power if that's what you're looking for). But the price model is ridiculous. If you want something free, Davinci Resolve is amazing.

2) What hardware specs do I need and if you have a computer to recommend that would be great as I am looking for a new one

I have 8gb of RAM, a 650 Ti BOOST, and an AMD 6300. You can get those parts for dirt cheap now a days. I can run Adobe Premier with 1080p video editing just fine.

I'm going to answer #2 first: The most important thing to do is have a balanced system. Don't have 32gb and an i3 or a $800 GPU and 4gb of ram. You should try to keep all of your components even so there are no bottle necks. That being said you should have: a cpu with hyperthreading, 8gb of ram and a 64bit OS, good cooling, A GPU supported by the programs you want to use (if you're building then read up on some software and find the best card that fits your needs). If you plan on gaming at all do not bye any quadro or Firepro cards.

Now for #1: I suggest you build your own computer. It is cheaper and you have more control. Plus you can make sure you have an even system! (see #2). Use either OSX or WINDOWS 7-8-10 (id say stay away from 10 though) There are no benefits from one OS to another. Use what you are comfy with. DaVinci Resolve Lite, Blender, and GIMP are good free tools to edit with. That being said, feel free to torrent and test other, more expensive software.

I don't want to come off as a bad influence, but if I hadn't torrented Adobe CS3 Creative Suite I would not be a editor in the same capacity I am today. Learn to torrent and try new software (DON'T JUST STICK TO ADOBE BECAUSE YOU TRIED IT FIRST!). Try things like C4D, Sony Vegas, Nuke Studio, and Maya.

This method is used if you want a clean install with none of the annoying factory partitions. It takes a little time (about an hour for completion), but it is worth it if you use your tablet as much as I do.

Dell now provides the drivers for including in a Windows image for the Venue 8 Pro.

I used a Windows 8.1 ISO and NTLite to create an image with the Dell drivers and a key (it was very simple and NTLite even has an option to read the embedded key from the system on install) and used a usb thumb drive to install it with (I have used a Windows 10 ISO as well, works great). I deleted all the partitions, and it left me with 19 - 20 GB usable after install.

This is the method I used: Fresh Windows 8.1 on Dell Venue 8 Pro, and it only took about an hour for preparation and install.

If you don't have a Windows 8.1 ISO, then you can make one here, fully supported my Microsoft and fully updated: Create Windows 8.1 ISO

I will warn you though, that if you choose to delete all the partitions, the recovery partition will be one of them, but if you keep the usb key with the ISO on it, then you won't need the recovery partition.

I am happy without the recovery partition now that I have created my own ISO with drivers that I can use on install. I have about 19 GB left, and I install all my programs on a class 10 SD card.

Some may say relativity is more difficult but generally to the common individual that has no training in either is not classed as not Intelligent is unfair.

With IQ tests where a variety of general tests are completed to measure intelligence is only a guide and not a solid measure as people who get a low score around 90 - 110 can still achieve a lot in life, such as gaining degrees and have a successful in their career of choice.

Disclaimer: As a 2nd year psych student I may not have accurately expressed the arguments to the full extent.

Depending on how one is defining intelligence, certainly and especially if you look at the biological side of the argument. Simply put, if your born with certain conditions--Like Down's--there's an automatic cap on your potential. There's a host of other things that could prevent development, like certain environmental factors, too. I also see the argument that @Greyseeker is making. How are we defining intelligence?
